findings.finding: Procurement's €3.0M applies 12% to €25M including €1.1M rush freight; the defensible figure is €2.87M a year (C0001). All headline numbers now trace to F/C ids; the check reports no unsupported number.
findings.action: Replaced €3.0M with €2.87M gross and €7.80M net 3-year; kept €3.0M only as the claim being tested

findings.finding: The fact extractor read the invoice column invoiced_eur_m as EUR with thousands separators (1.444 -> 1,444 EUR). Monthly invoice totals are therefore not used in any headline; only rush-freight values (parsed correctly) and finance's 23.9 / 1.1 EUR M are used.
findings.action: Recorded in fact_conflicts.json; manual reconciliation: incumbent 17.83 + Supplier B 7.17 = 25.0 EUR M, rush freight sums to 1.10 EUR M, consistent with finance note

findings.finding: A pure 'reject' would leave the board without an approvable alternative and leave €1.79M a year on the table.
findings.action: Added costed options (status quo, full move, 70/30), asks with owners, three gates and four KPIs; the current plan is tested and its cost if kept (€1.07M over three years under repeat stoppages) stated

findings.finding: The gap of €1.21M a year to procurement's €3.0M must be admitted, not hidden.
findings.action: Gap stated with how it could be closed (rush freight via forecasting, upper bound to be sized) and why price cannot close it

findings.finding: The risk case rests on two historical stoppages; a single 14-day stoppage (€2.4M) would NOT erase the full move's €2.93M advantage. If Supplier B has a credible fix for its force-majeure causes, the full move could be right.
findings.action: Caveat added to I2 and hypothesis H4 rationale; continuity gate (Q1 2027) and 2028 revisit gate make the single-sourcing option reopenable on evidence (second plant or tested coverage of a 14-day stoppage)

findings.finding: The 70/30 split still leaves 70% of volume on Supplier B's single plant; its stoppage loss is not quantified in the sources.
findings.action: Stated as a caveat; the incumbent already producing 30% across two plants and able to cover up to 60% is a materially better position than starting from zero; continuity gate tests the ramp-up

findings.finding: Volume breaks might be negotiable (e.g. 9% at 70% could be improved); options use only quoted terms.
findings.action: Kept quoted terms only (no invented data); contract gate requires written confirmation

findings.finding: Rush-freight slide (S6) could be cut, but without it the board asks where the rest of the €3.0M went; kept as core but short.
No slide-level deck.json yet (render spec); scope of this pass is storyline and deck plan.
findings.action: Answered: render spec is out of scope for this storyline deliverable
